Get started with niceSMD

Source: vignettes/niceSMD.Rmd
niceSMD.Rmd

niceSMD builds a “Table 1” of descriptive statistics for two or more groups, with one absolute standardized mean difference (SMD) per variable, and shows it as a formatted table in the console, in Quarto and R Markdown documents, and in editable Word files.

library(niceSMD)
d <- example_table1_data()
head(d, 3)
#>     group age  bmi    sex smoking stage_code analysis_weight stratum cluster
#> 1 Control  43 20.3 Female   Never          1             1.6   North       1
#> 2 Control  50 21.6   Male    <NA>          1             2.7   South       2
#> 3 Control  57 22.9   <NA> Current          2             3.8   North       3

A first table

Name the grouping column and the covariates to summarize. When more than two groups are present, group_for_SMD names the pair the SMD compares; all groups are still displayed.

tab <- nice_SMD_table1(
  d, group = "group",
  covar_names = c("age", "bmi", "sex", "smoking", "stage_code"),
  print_covariate_names = c("Age (years)", "BMI", "Sex", "Smoking", "Stage"),
  categorical_vars = "stage_code",           # numeric codes -> categories
  group_for_SMD = c("Control", "Treatment"),
  show_missing = "if_any",                   # Missing rows only where needed
  notes = "short"                            # compact footnote
)
tab

Categorical variables: n (%) among nonmissing values. Continuous variables: mean (SD) and median (Q1, Q3). Missing: n (% of group).

SMD = absolute standardized mean difference (Control vs. Treatment); NE = not estimable.

Ending a chunk with the object (as above) prints the formatted table in HTML, Word, and PDF output. Variable names are bold, categories are indented, and the footnotes appear below the table.

What you get back

tab is a list. The pieces you will use most:

tab$smd[, c("label", "smd", "status")]   # numeric, unrounded SMDs
#>         label        smd status
#> 1 Age (years) 3.45103284     ok
#> 2         BMI 3.48239000     ok
#> 3         Sex 0.00000000     ok
#> 4     Smoking 0.09313035     ok
#> 5       Stage 0.21601820     ok
tab$groups                               # group sizes
#>       group  n sum_weights effective_n
#> 1   Control 30          30          30
#> 2 Treatment 30          30          30
#> 3  Registry 30          30          30

The options you will use most

Goal Argument
Show a Missing row only for variables that have missing values show_missing = "if_any"
Hide or always show all Missing rows show_missing = FALSE / TRUE
Short, manuscript-style footnote notes = "short" (or "none")
Analysis weights weights = "analysis_weight"
Complex survey design design = survey::svydesign(...)
Fewer or more decimals contDigits, catDigits, smdDigits
Order of group columns group_order = c(...)

See ?nice_SMD_table1 for every argument with examples.

Export to Word 

save_table1_docx(tab, "Table1.docx", landscape = FALSE, font_size = 10)

Or pass docx_path = "Table1.docx" to nice_SMD_table1(). Use table1_flextable() to get an editable flextable for further styling.

Several trials?

For pooled individual participant data from multiple trials, see nice_trial_table1() and the article Tables by trial and treatment arm.
